claim:
For the constant-temperature compound-Poisson development process \(X_t=c t+\sum_{j=1}^{N_t}G_j\), with \(c,\lambda,\theta>0\), \(N_t\) Poisson of rate \(\lambda\), and i.i.d. jumps \(G_j\sim\operatorname{Exp}(\text{scale }\theta)\), let \(\tau_x=\inf\{t>0:X_t\ge x\}\) and \(O_x=X_{\tau_x}-x\). Writing \(\kappa=(c+\lambda\theta)/(c\theta)\), one has \(\mathbb P(O_x=0)=c/(c+\lambda\theta)+(\lambda\theta/(c+\lambda\theta))e^{-\kappa x}\) and \(\mathbb E O_x=(\lambda\theta^2/(c+\lambda\theta))(1-e^{-\kappa x})\). Hence for every \(0\le a<b<\infty\),
\[
(c+\lambda\theta)\,\mathbb E(\tau_b-\tau_a)=(b-a)+\frac{\lambda\theta^2}{c+\lambda\theta}\bigl(e^{-\kappa a}-e^{-\kappa b}\bigr)>(b-a).
\]
Therefore the calibration identity used in Perçin et al., \(c=(b-a)/\mathbb E(\tau_b-\tau_a)-\lambda\theta\), is not valid for finite stage boundaries when \(\lambda\theta>0\); the missing term is the increase of the unconditional mean overshoot between the two levels.
integrity: All source-specific statements were checked against the public preprint or journal text. The proof is analytic; the bundled computation only replays closed-form identities. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The closed form assumes constant positive drift, Poisson jump arrivals, exponential positive jumps, and finite thresholds. It corrects the source-specific first-passage calibration but does not re-fit data or analyze the full temperature-dependent system. Equivalent special-case transforms may exist in general Lévy fluctuation literature.
title: Creeping makes the compound-Poisson stage calibration level-dependent
